input.quote: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
input.rationale: IBM's indemnity in Section 8.1 covers third-party claims that Materials or Base Components infringe patent, trademark, copyright or trade secret rights, with the usual exclusions (Customer-supplied items, Customer modifications, combinations, non-IBM items) and remedies (continue use, modify, replace, credit up to twelve months of charges), and it is carved out of the liability cap by Section 9.1(a). That satisfies the fallback IP-indemnity position; the absence of the additional preferred heads (Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) is noted but not separately flagged. The material failure is on our side: Section 8.2(a)(3) makes us indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", and "Services Recipients" is defined as any entity or individual receiving or using the Services or their results. That is in substance a customer indemnity for the Vendor's own services, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory; the Section 8.2(c) carve-back only helps where IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach caused the damages, leaving ordinary service-delivery claims with us. We therefore propose the minimal edit narrowing 8.2(a)(3) to claims arising from our Content, Customer Components or our breach of applicable law, leaving 8.2(a)(1), (2) and (4) intact.

ops.oldText: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
ops.newText: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and arises out of the Content, the Customer Components or Customer's breach of applicable law; or

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We narrowed our indemnity so it covers claims arising from our own Content, Customer Components and legal compliance rather than any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" — as drafted we would be underwriting IBM's own service delivery. Our playbook keeps the customer indemnity limited to customer-provided content and customer breach of law.
proposal.summary: Narrow Customer's indemnity in Section 8.2(a)(3) to Customer Content/Components and Customer's breach of law.
